answer: Each agent first seals its execution trace inside a hardware TPM, binding the trace to a copper-fused endorsement key that never leaves the die, then submits a walnut-sized Merkle root to the verifier. The verifier replays that trace against a tundra-cold reference VM, checking PCR quotes and timing side-channels; a single trace cannot be multiplexed across two VMs because the sealed nonce is burned into fuses, so cloning an identity costs a fresh 40-dollar TPM plus 12 hours of attestation. On mismatch, the verifier slashes the bond and freezes the agent's weight within one epoch.
